description: Apply the federation ADR (chief/51) into the three specs that each defer the single-authority question, turning three separate 'future option' notes into one consistent, ADR-backed clause per spec (ROADMAP.md Phase F1): KINP §11 (identity-authority role -> federated authorities, identity.md ~line 477), KCB §7.1 (single registry -> peering registries, capability-bus.md ~line 251), and KMI §9 (single CAS -> per-project stores replicating on reference, media-interchange.md ~line 380). Each edit is normative, so per koine's draft->candidate->ratified convention each touched spec bumps version and returns to candidate pending the multi-authority pressure test (chief/53). PARKED: gated on chief/51 and on a real >1-authority deployment target (ROADMAP.md: 'nothing is built until a deployment actually needs more than one authority'). Public-safe/agnostic: bind roles, names no deployment.
verify: python3 -c "import json,glob; [json.load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('schemas/*.json')]; print('schemas ok')"

userStories.title: KINP §11 — identity-authority role generalized to federated authorities
userStories.description: Edit identity.md §11 (the resolver-authority fork, ~line 477) to apply the ADR: keep the single authority ROLE as the default, and specify the federated-authorities extension the ADR resolves, citing the ADR instead of restating a bespoke 'future option'.
acceptanceCriteria: identity.md §11 references the federation ADR (chief/51) and specifies how the single identity-authority role generalizes to federated authorities, preserving the offline-first minting and authority-as-role invariants (§6, §11).
The KINP version header is bumped and Status set to candidate, with a changelog entry citing the ADR; cross-references to §11 elsewhere in the spec stay consistent.
The change is additive to the existing model — a single-authority deployment stays conformant unchanged.

userStories.title: KCB §7.1 — single registry generalized to peering registries
userStories.description: Edit capability-bus.md §7 open question 1 (~line 251) to apply the ADR: the single host-provisioned discovery registry generalizes to per-org registries that peer, citing the ADR.
acceptanceCriteria: capability-bus.md's registry-federation clause references the ADR and specifies the peering-registries extension, consistent with ADR-0001's route-by-lookup-not-proxy stance (the registry returns addresses; peers dial each other).
The KCB version header is bumped and Status set to candidate, with a changelog entry citing the ADR.
A single-registry deployment stays conformant unchanged (additive).

userStories.title: KMI §9 — single CAS generalized to per-project stores replicating on reference
userStories.description: Edit media-interchange.md §9 open question 3 / the CAS operational model (~line 380) to apply the ADR: a single shared content-addressed store generalizes to per-project stores that replicate on reference.
acceptanceCriteria: media-interchange.md's CAS clause references the ADR and specifies the per-project-store-replicating-on-reference model, keeping content-addressed asset identity byte-stable across stores.
The KMI version header is bumped and Status set to candidate, with a changelog entry citing the ADR; the three edited specs read consistently with each other and all cite the one ADR.

The three §-edits leave every current single-authority deployment conformant (the fold is additive), and each names chief/53-multi-authority-scenario as the pressure test that must break-test the shared pattern before re-ratification.
